BBC News, published 19 Nov 2026 06:05 GMT

Protest hotel to end asylum seeker accommodation

The Potters International Hotel in Aldershot is among eight hotels which will no longer accommodate asylum seekers

Exterior view of red brick hotel with car park in front. Police van is parked in the car park.

A hotel which was the scene of a violent anti-immigration protest in 2024 is set to stop housing asylum seekers, the government has confirmed.

More than 200 people gathered at the Potters International Hotel in Aldershot, Hampshire, in July 2024. Eight people - including a 13-year-old girl - were sentenced for their role in disturbances that followed.

The incident was part of the rioting that swept across England in the days after the fatal stabbing of three young girls in Southport.

It is among eight asylum hotels across the UK which will stop housing asylum seekers, which the government said was due to a \"significant drop\" in small boat arrivals and speedier asylum decision making.

The Home Office said a total of 52 hotels have closed so far this year, leaving around 140 open – down from 400 at the 2023 peak.

The number of people in asylum hotels has halved in a year to 16,000.

It said while claims are considered, rather than staying in costly hotels, asylum seekers were being moved to alternative and more basic forms of accommodation, including former military barracks.

The latest closures are expected to reduce asylum costs by around £16m.

They include the Roundhouse Hotel in Bournemouth which the government said earlier this year that it intended to empty.

It has brought the number of asylum seekers in hotels in the Dorset town down to 120 from 600, according to Tom Hayes, Labour MP for Bournemouth East.

Border security and asylum minister, Anna Turley, said: \"This government is restoring fairness and control to an immigration system that had spiralled out of control, with hundreds of expensive asylum hotels opened up across the country.

\"Thanks to our reforms, small boat arrivals and asylum claims are down while processing and removals are up, meaning thousands fewer asylum seekers are relying on taxpayer-funded support.

\"That is why more hotels are closing and we won't stop until they are all shut for good.\"

Following the ending of asylum seeker accommodation in a number of other hotels earlier this year, the Conservatives said the government was \"shunting people from hotels into residential apartments to hide what is going on\".

More than 200 people gathered at the hotel in Aldershot on 31 July 2024

The protest at the hotel on 31 July 2024 followed the fatal stabbing of three girls in Southport - with unrest fuelled by misinformation online.

More than 200 people gathered at the hotel. A small group entered the car park, kicked footballs against windows, damaged blinds and a perimeter wall, set off flares and threw bicycles into a skip.

The 13-year-old girl, who could be named because of her age, was filmed punching and kicking a glass door at the hotel.

There were other outbreaks of violence in a number of towns and cities across England and in Northern Ireland, including Plymouth, Sunderland, Belfast, Rotherham, Manchester and London.
